$comment: Copy to ~/.pi-jupyter/config.json — env vars take precedence over this file.
$comment.kernelName: OPTIONAL fallback default kernel ONLY. Which kernel (python3 / ir / …) serves a notebook is decided when the notebook is OPENED: a live kernel wins, then the agent's `kernel` param on jupyter_open_notebook, then the kernelspec recorded in the notebook file, then this fallback. It is never chosen on jupyter_repl / jupyter_add_dependencies / jupyter_save_notebook calls. Must be a kernelspec *name* (see GET /api/kernelspecs): e.g. "python3", or "ir" for R — NOT a display name like "R".
$comment.purposes: What each kernel is for lives SEPARATELY in ~/.pi-jupyter/purposes.json (a JSON map like {"python3": "data analysis"}). The agent records it with jupyter_set_kernel_purpose after you explain a new kernel; you may also edit that file by hand. It only describes kernels, never selects one.
$comment.notebooks: Which notebooks pi has opened is remembered in ~/.pi-jupyter/notebooks.json (contents path -> kernel/last-used). jupyter_list_notebooks merges it with the server's live sessions so a NEW conversation can continue a notebook — attaching to its still-running kernel when there is one, otherwise starting a new kernel bound to the same path and re-running the file's cells from first to last so the state is restored.
$comment.extras: Optional fields: "workingDir": "/path/to/project" (base for relative save paths), "timeoutRestartKernel": true (auto-restart a kernel still busy after a timeout; state is lost), "bindSession": true (bind the kernel to an /api/sessions row so it shows up in the Jupyter Running UI; defaults to true), and "keepKernels": false (kill named-notebook kernels when the pi conversation ends instead of leaving them running for re-attach; defaults to true).
$comment.remoteAutoSave: After each jupyter_repl cell, automatically upload the notebook snapshot to the remote server (Contents API). Defaults to true; set false to disable. The file lands at the contents root == the remote $HOME in a default deployment, under <notebookId>.ipynb (or under a path you opened with jupyter_open_notebook), so opening it in a browser reuses the SAME kernel.
$comment.remoteSavePath: Legacy override of the remote contents path, used ONLY for sessions created without an explicit path — every session today opens a named notebook (jupyter_open_notebook / the required `notebook` param), so this is rarely used. Empty string == default <notebookId>.ipynb. ".." segments are rejected.
